title: Questions 176-180 refer to the following e-mail and review.
passage_1:
From:Emeka Duruji <duruji@highlandridgecoffee.com>
To:Beatriz Salgado <b.salgado@norwoodcafegroup.com>
Date:October 6
Subject:Harvest Notice and Account Update

Dear Ms. Salgado,

I would like to inform you regarding your order for our signature Amber Peak Beans. Because of the unusual heavy rain this autumn, the picking has been slightly delayed. You will probably receive your shipment early next month. I should point out that this will not be a concern in later seasons. We are presently building shaded drying decks across our property. This will let us stretch our processing window into early winter and protect the harvest from harsh conditions in the future.

In addition, we are upgrading our trade buyer portal. Please sign in before Friday to confirm that the following records are accurate:

  • Import Permit Number
  • Delivery Address
  • Purchasing Officer Name

To reward our loyal buyers, we have revised our freight policy: any wholesale order above $600 will now be sent at no delivery cost.

Best regards,
Emeka Duruji
Director of Sales, Highland Ridge Coffee

Buyer: Norwood Café Group (Beatriz Salgado)
Date: October 24
Product Reviewed: Amber Peak Beans (Batch #718)

Even though the shipment came four days later than originally scheduled, I was genuinely impressed by the quality of the beans. They were far less bitter than I had anticipated. They suit our new winter blend perfectly. To keep their aroma, I advise grinding the beans only once, right before brewing.

I was also pleased that our order reached us with no freight charge. Having the delivery cost waived on such a premium batch was a real advantage for our cafés.
